title: Principal Engineer at Semtech Corporation Believes Marvell’s Lumentum Acquisition Is Strategically Sound but Carries Integration Risks
expert: Principal engineer at Semtech (current; competitor in EICs/drivers, supplier to Lumentum transceivers)
verdict: A Semtech principal engineer (competitor and Lumentum supplier, opinion-led) calls the deal the right full-stack move for 1.6T–6.4T optics against Broadcom, but warns it dilutes Marvell's around 67% fabless margins with fab capex in the hundreds of millions.

Greenfield legs: InP laser capacity bought up roughly three years, to around 2029 (estimate), first read; ownership secures supply. → Tenet 3 (scale-up optics) ↑
Margins: around 67% fabless margins at risk from fab capex (estimate); the expert's 67% is above reported non-GAAP GM of 58.9% (SB #65481): conflicting baseline. → Tenet 4 (GM dilution) ↓
Interconnect growth rate: no significant immediate impact on Marvell's DSP business (estimate); Credo gains as the neutral supplier. → Tenet 2 (1.6T duopoly) →

changes: First read on Lumentum laser capacity (bought up roughly three years, to around 2029); no earlier expert call or stored row.
Fabless margin around 67% (estimate) vs reported Q2 FY27 non-GAAP GM 58.9% (SB #65481): conflicting (expert overstates the base).
Combined company "say" two-thirds / 66% for Marvell (estimate) vs MRVL holders ~67% (SB #67098): consistent.
thesis_impact: Tenet 3 (scale-up optics greenfield): ↑ — full stack of electronics, photonic fabric and lasers needed for 1.6T and 3.2/6.4T; InP capacity secured to around 2029.
Tenet 4 (opex leverage > GM dilution): ↓ — fab capex in the hundreds of millions and high-power lasers in the billions dilute fabless margins.
Tenet 2 (1.6T duopoly): → — no significant immediate impact expected on the DSP business.
Tenet 5 (bear flank): ↑ — integration over more than a year and heavy debt; dismantling Lumentum's management could be disastrous.
